Task: Format method Javadocs as multi-line blocks
commitResults.messageBody:
The markAsDone() and markAsNotDone() methods in Task use single-line
Javadoc comments.

Single-line Javadoc comments for methods are inconsistent with the
multi-line Javadoc format used across other methods in the class and
the SE-EDU coding standards.

Let's convert the Javadoc comments on markAsDone() and markAsNotDone()
into multi-line blocks.

Standardizing the method Javadoc formatting improves readability and
maintains codebase style consistency.

Coding standard instructions are previously tracked in a standalone
markdown document and referenced in AGENTS.md.

Having coding standards encapsulated as an agent skill enables AI
assistants to automatically discover and adhere to the project's Java
coding conventions during development.

Let's:
* create the seedu-java-coding-standard skill definition
* update AGENTS.md to mandate following the skill
* remove the obsolete CODING_STANDARDS.md entry from .gitignore

This centralizes Java styling guidelines under the SE-EDU standard.

Git conventions for commit messages and branch naming are not
systematically enforced for AI assistant interactions.

Without an explicit git standard skill, generated commit messages and
branch names may not follow the SE-EDU project conventions.

Let's:
* create the seedu-git-standard skill based on SE-EDU conventions
* update AGENTS.md to mandate following this skill for all commits

This ensures consistent commit message structure and branch naming.
